::: {.callout-note title="Evidence"}
This page summarizes exported entry points and orchestration at
`3b4c05386e5a44d05633136ecbcf5dd067f70435`. Form behaviour, destructive
operations, Office automation, files, and database effects require runtime
verification with non-production data.
:::

## Classifications

`cmdClassifications` exposes view and manage entry points for the base and
exchange database roles. It loads key families, classifications,
dimension-to-classification mappings, descriptions, and table definitions into
`clsDB` collections, then initializes `frmClassification` in view or manage
mode.

| Form outcome | Source workflow |
|---|---|
| New | Create a classification workbook with a save command. |
| Edit | Create and fill a workbook from the selected classification. |
| Export | Delegate to `ExportClassifications`. |
| Remove | Implemented by form and save modules; descriptions and dimension references require explicit review. |

`TestClassLen` compares classification code lengths with dimensions that use
the classification and warns about values that do not fit. It is an application
check, not a database relationship.

## Correspondences

`cmdCorrespondence.ViewCorrespondences` and `ManageCorrespondences` both load
correspondences and classifications, then initialize `frmCorrespondence` with a
view/manage flag. Manage mode can collect source/target classification names,
open `frmCorrespondanceEdit`, generate an editing workbook, fill it from the
database, or export correspondences.

This source fills the placeholders left in the retained draft, but does not yet
provide a complete rule contract. Required tests include duplicate mappings,
missing source/target codes, many-to-one and one-to-many mappings, deletion,
round-trip export, and use during aggregated load operations.

## Key families and dimensions

`cmdKeyFamily` provides base and exchange workflows for viewing, creating, and
managing key families. The forms load key-family names and dimensions, check
that each named table exists, and expose operations such as delete, remove data,
conditional remove, dimension-length modification, and workbook export.

Creation is completed by form code calling `DbCreateTables.CreateNewKeyFam` and
adding the name to `KeyNames`. Deletion removes both the name and its table.
These are destructive schema operations and require backup, authorization,
transaction, and recovery tests.

`cmdDimensions` loads key families, dimensions, dimension classifications, and
classifications before opening `frmDimensions`. The retained draft lists remove
classification, code inspection, and validation actions; those actions live in
the form and related classes and should be tested before being treated as a
stable administrative API.

## Batch processing

`cmdBatchRun.BatchUpdate` loads workbook and batch metadata and opens
`frmBatchRun`. `BatchRun.DoBatchUpdate` then executes the selected ordered
workbook list.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  select["Select batch and run options"]
  preflight["Load metadata and reject reserved, transferred, or exported workbooks"]
  open["Open next registered workbook"]
  validate["Load globals/year and validate definitions"]
  load["Load data"]
  save["Save data"]
  close["Optionally close workbook and log timing"]
  repeat{"Changes saved and repetitions remain?"}
  finish["Restore Excel visibility and stop log"]

  select --> preflight --> open --> validate
  validate --> load --> save --> close --> repeat
  repeat -->|"Yes"| open
  repeat -->|"No"| finish
```

The workflow can run silently, hide Excel, display a modeless progress form,
repeat until no values are saved or a configured limit is reached, and close
workbooks. It also contains an option to terminate Dropbox before processing.
Process termination, hidden Excel state, partially completed batches, formula
handling, cancellation, logging, and restart behaviour are security and
recoverability concerns; test them explicitly.

## Design tools

`cmdDesign` and `cmdShowHide` implement the design ribbon group:

| Command | Source behaviour |
|---|---|
| Test design | Call `TestDefinitions` for the active base or exchange definitions. |
| Mark definition areas | Validate, remove existing colours, and apply configured colours to referenced areas. |
| Get column names | Resolve a key family and insert dimension/classification information into the workbook. |
| Add row | Extend `DBLinks` or `ExchLinks` by one row. |
| Create links | Create a definition sheet, headings, and initial named range. |
| Fill global names | Load `DBGlobals` and create/fill missing workbook structures where supported. |
| Clear database for workbook | Delete key-family rows attributed to the current workbook after validation and confirmation. |
| Clean up names | Collect names referenced by NADABAS structures and offer to remove unused workbook names. |
| Hide/show templates | Change definition-sheet visibility, including administrator-sensitive hiding. |

“Clear” and “clean up” are destructive operations. Their selection boundaries,
confirmation text, and recovery path need manual tests.

## Administration and settings

| Area | Main source | Behaviour and caveat |
|---|---|---|
| Administrators | `cmdAdministrators`, `frmAdministrators` | Load and edit the `Administrators` table; `TestAdministrator` sets session state from Windows user identity. |
| Permissions | `cmdPermissions`, `frmPermissions`, `clsPermission` | Load and edit per-workbook user rows; `TestPermissionForUser` influences `clsWBData.ReadOnly`. This is application authorization, not a database access-control guarantee. |
| User settings | `cmdUserSettings`, `frmUserSettings`, `clsUserSettings` | Load/save database-held colours, workbook policies, passwords, load/save options, and feature flags. Scope and one-row assumptions need deployment verification. |
| Years | `cmdSetYears` | Store period name, bounds, and format; set scan-time period state and validate values. Locale and non-calendar formats require tests. |
| Globals | `cmdGlobals` | Edit database global variables and fill workbook `DBGlobals` before data operations. |
| Base folder | `cmdBaseFolder` | Set and resolve the portable file root; Access initialization can use the database folder. |
| Workbook status | `cmdWorkBookStatus` | Display registered workbook metadata and file-existence checks; list reserved workbooks. |
| Version | `cmdVersion`, `InterfaceVersionUpdate` | Recreate/update `NADABASVersion`, compare the running add-in version with the database, execute legacy repair checks, and schedule the administrator-controlled public GitHub release check once per week. A newer release produces a translated Yes/No prompt that can open the NADABAS download page; the administration menu also provides a manual check and shared on/off toggle. No file is downloaded or installed automatically. |
| Workbook passwords | `cmdSetRemovePassword`, protection modules | Apply or remove a shared workbook password across registered files. Storage and use of workbook passwords require a security decision. |

The retained draft says database-held settings ensure consistency across all
users. The source does centralize them, but consistency still depends on the
database selected, write permissions, caching, concurrency, and when each
session reloads values.

## Backup and restore

`cmdBackupPath.SetBackUpFolder` stores a backup folder/template and prevents
choosing a location below the base path. `cmdBackUp.DoBackUp` creates a
timestamped folder and either copies the entire base folder or copies selected
registered workbooks. For Access it can copy the `.accdb` file. For SQL Server,
the source creates an Access file and delegates table copying through
`cmdConvertDB.DOBackupSQL`; this is a logical export, not a native SQL Server
backup.

`DoRestore` copies a selected database file and registered workbooks back into
their target locations. Its implementation is file-oriented and should not be
assumed to restore a SQL Server database.

::: {.callout-warning title="Backup is not verified recovery"}
A success message or completed file copy does not establish a recoverable,
consistent backup. Define supported Access and SQL Server procedures, test
restore into an isolated environment, reconcile row counts and key families,
and document retention, encryption, access control, and disaster-recovery
ownership.
:::

## Access and SQL Server conversion

`cmdConvertDB` contains Access-to-SQL and SQL-to-Access workflows. It creates a
target `clsDB`, switches `CurrentDB` between source and target, creates required
tables, copies optional system tables, reconstructs key-family tables, and moves
data through recordsets.

Conversion changes schema and data and must be treated as a migration:

- take and verify a recoverable source backup;
- prevent concurrent writers;
- record source/target engine and provider versions;
- compare table, row, key, null, text, date, and numeric values;
- verify indexes and application behaviour;
- retain logs without credentials or confidential data;
- define rollback before starting.

## Debugging and diagnostics

`cmdTrace` creates a trace workbook and records workbook, table, timing, and
cell-level changes during load operations. `cmdSQLLog` creates a workbook and
appends SQL text while logging is active. `BatchLog` records batch timing and
operation information.

These tools can expose statistical values, paths, SQL, user names, and database
structure. Use only non-production data unless an approved handling procedure
defines access, storage, redaction, and deletion. Do not attach unreviewed trace
or SQL-log workbooks to public issues.

## Operational verification backlog

- define role and permission matrices for ordinary users and administrators;
- characterize every destructive form action and its confirmation/recovery;
- test batch cancellation and Excel/process recovery at every stage;
- approve supported backup/restore procedures separately for Access and SQL
  Server;
- validate migrations with repeatable reconciliation reports;
- define safe diagnostic collection and redaction;
- replace implicit shared state with explicit interfaces before extracting a
  workflow into .NET.
